subject: Linear Algebra
title: Orthogonal Diagonalization, Positive Definite Matrices, QR and SVD
note: Original ACADRIX practice MCQs based on the R-2025 Unit IV syllabus. These are not official Anna University questions or PYQs.

questions.q: A real matrix A is symmetric when:
questions.explanation: A real square matrix is symmetric if it equals its transpose.

questions.q: A real symmetric matrix can be orthogonally diagonalized into a matrix whose diagonal entries are:
questions.explanation: The spectral theorem states that a real symmetric matrix is orthogonally diagonalizable with real eigenvalues.

questions.q: In an orthogonal diagonalization A=QDQᵀ, Q satisfies:
questions.explanation: The columns of Q form an orthonormal eigenvector basis, so Q is orthogonal.

questions.q: For an orthogonal matrix Q, Q⁻¹ equals:
questions.explanation: Orthogonal matrices satisfy QᵀQ=I, hence Q⁻¹=Qᵀ.

questions.q: The columns of an orthogonal matrix are:
questions.explanation: An orthogonal matrix has mutually orthogonal unit-length columns.

questions.q: For a symmetric matrix, eigenvectors corresponding to distinct eigenvalues are:
questions.explanation: Distinct eigenspaces of a real symmetric matrix are orthogonal.

questions.q: A symmetric matrix is positive definite if:
questions.explanation: Positive definiteness is defined by a strictly positive quadratic form for every nonzero vector.

questions.q: For a positive definite matrix A, all eigenvalues are:
questions.explanation: A real symmetric positive definite matrix has strictly positive eigenvalues.

questions.q: A positive definite matrix must be:
questions.explanation: All eigenvalues of a positive definite matrix are positive, so none is zero and the matrix is invertible.

questions.q: For a 2×2 symmetric matrix, positive definiteness can be checked using positive:
questions.explanation: Sylvester's criterion states that all leading principal minors must be positive.

questions.q: The QR decomposition factors a matrix A as:
questions.explanation: QR decomposition writes A as the product of an orthogonal matrix Q and an upper triangular matrix R.

questions.q: In a QR decomposition A=QR, Q is generally:
questions.explanation: Q contains an orthonormal basis for the column space when using the standard reduced/full QR construction.

questions.q: In a standard QR decomposition of a square matrix, R is:
questions.explanation: The R factor is constructed as an upper triangular matrix from the orthonormalization process.

questions.q: QR decomposition can be obtained using the:
questions.explanation: Applying Gram-Schmidt to the columns of A produces orthonormal columns of Q and the corresponding R factor.

questions.q: The singular value decomposition of A has the form:
questions.explanation: SVD factors A into orthogonal/unitary matrices U and V and a diagonal nonnegative singular-value matrix Σ.

questions.q: The entries on the diagonal of the SVD matrix Σ are called:
questions.explanation: The diagonal entries of Σ are the singular values, conventionally nonnegative.

questions.q: The singular values of A are related to the eigenvalues of:
questions.explanation: The singular values are the nonnegative square roots of the eigenvalues of AᵀA.

questions.q: The singular values of a matrix are always:
questions.explanation: Singular values are defined as nonnegative square roots of eigenvalues of AᵀA.

questions.q: The rank of a matrix equals the number of:
questions.explanation: The rank of A is the number of positive/nonzero singular values in its SVD.

questions.q: In A=UΣVᵀ, the columns of U are called:
questions.explanation: Columns of U are left singular vectors, while columns of V are right singular vectors.

questions.q: In A=UΣVᵀ, the columns of V are called:
questions.explanation: The columns of V form the right singular-vector basis.

questions.q: A least-squares solution minimizes the:
questions.explanation: Least squares chooses x to minimize ||Ax−b||².

questions.q: For an overdetermined system Ax≈b, the normal equations are:
questions.explanation: Differentiating the squared residual norm gives the normal equations AᵀAx=Aᵀb.

questions.q: If A has full column rank, the least-squares solution is unique because:
questions.explanation: Full column rank makes AᵀA positive definite and therefore invertible.

questions.q: The least-squares residual r=b−Ax is orthogonal to the:
questions.explanation: The normal equations imply Aᵀ(b−Ax)=0, so the residual is orthogonal to every column of A.

questions.q: The orthogonal projection of b onto Col(A) is:
options: Ax̂ for a least-squares solution x̂
questions.answer: Ax̂ for a least-squares solution x̂
questions.explanation: The least-squares approximation Ax̂ is the orthogonal projection of b onto the column space of A.

questions.q: For a symmetric matrix, orthogonal diagonalization uses an orthonormal basis of:
questions.explanation: The spectral theorem provides an orthonormal eigenvector basis for a real symmetric matrix.

questions.q: If Q is orthogonal, multiplication by Q preserves the:
questions.explanation: Orthogonal transformations preserve lengths because ||Qx||²=xᵀQᵀQx=xᵀx.

questions.q: The Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse can be used to obtain a least-squares solution when a system is:
questions.explanation: The pseudoinverse provides a least-squares solution for general systems, including inconsistent ones.

questions.q: For A=UΣVᵀ, U and V are:
options: Orthogonal matrices in the real case
questions.answer: Orthogonal matrices in the real case
questions.explanation: For a real matrix, the SVD uses orthogonal U and V with UᵀU=I and VᵀV=I.
